meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law codified system with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation and limited Common Law-inspired commercial modifications)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–United Arab Emirates Bilateral Investment Treaty

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Anti-Money Laundering as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 8 of 2015; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 148 of 2019; Prime Ministerial Decree No. 44 of 2020 on the Ultimate Beneficial Owner Register; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT regulations and Unified Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each natural-person shareholder's passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country Ministry of Interior / Passport Authority and local notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing for each corporate shareholder
Board resolution approving the Egyptian investment, appointing local counsel, and designating signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary and board of directors of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney to the local formation agent / law firm
Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for each shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit sanctions and terrorist financing lists, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the domestic database of politically exposed persons maintained by the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Continuous transaction monitoring, negative news screening, and risk-based client classification are mandatory under Law No. 80 of 2002 and the Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Companies Registration Online Portal and the Egyptian Unified Electronic Commercial Registry / Commercial Registry of Cairo Governorate
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every Egyptian LLC name must be stated in Arabic using the Arabic alphabet. A Latin-script transliteration may be registered only as an additional translation; all statutory filings and legal notices must reference the Arabic name. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names, and foreign-word transliterations are subject to GAFI consistency review.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name clearance may be extended once for 30 days by submitting a written request through the GAFI investor portal prior to expiry. On rejection, the applicant receives a written reason and may file an administrative appeal with GAFI's Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution Committee within 15 days of the rejection notice, attaching a memorandum and a proposed alternative name. If the Committee rejects again, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Cairo Administrative Court. The initial administrative appeal is free; public counsel fees are incurred only upon filing for judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where a registered agent packages and maintains a physical, serviceable Egyptian address for receipt of legal process and tax notices; remote or mail-forwarding-only virtual arrangements are not accepted by GAFI or the Egyptian Tax Authority. For ISIC 6201 Cybersecurity SaaS, serviced offices and shared business centers are generally accepted provided they offer a physical meeting room, records storage, and letter-before-inspection processing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 18 months, primarily triggered by VAT registration irregularities, documented office-address discrepancies, or AML/CFT red-flag filings; otherwise, regulatory supervision is desk-based.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 194 of 2020, as amended, and Executive Regulations issued under Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 2022, including the provisions governing Limited Liability Companies and Company Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Investor Services Center (One-Stop-Shop), in coordination with the Commercial Registry of the Company's Governorate
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Contract of Incorporation (Memorandum and Articles of Association) executed before a licensed notary and filed with GAFI
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for Egyptian LLCs under Law 194/2020; the partners must fix a capital amount adequate for the corporate object and fully subscribe it at formation. In-kind contributions (e.g., software source code and intangibles) must be fully paid at incorporation and certified by a licensed valuer, whereas cash contributions may be paid in installments within five years with any unpaid balance recorded as a shareholder receivable. A bank deposit certificate (escrow-style capital account) must evidence the cash portion paid at formation for GAFI validation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the capital of the Company is fully subscribed by the founding Members as set out in the notarized Articles of Association, and the paid-up capital position is affirmed. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office at [address], Cairo, Egypt, is adopted as the Company's statutory seat. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed General Manager and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, with authority to sign agreements, operate bank accounts, and file returns. RESOLVED FINALLY, that the managers shall obtain all registrations and licensing required for cybersecurity cloud operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Corporate Name and File Pre-Formation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center (One-Stop-Shop) and the GAFI online incorporation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request containing three ranked alternative trade names in Arabic and romanized form, each reflecting the cybersecurity SaaS activity. Verify the proposed name against the commercial register and protected designations. Pay the non-refundable name reservation fee and obtain the official name reservation certificate before proceeding to deed preparation.
required_dossiers: Original passport or national ID copies of all founding shareholders
Initial signed declaration of proposed corporate name, object, and capital
Power of attorney for the formation agent or law firm (if any)
Proof of intended registered office district
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, the applicant is entitled to receive the written refusal grounds and may substitute the next ranked alternative name without additional fee within 30 days; a disputed refusal may be submitted to GAFI's Legal Affairs Department for administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Notarize the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI-approved Notary Public and the incorporated legal counsel of the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Arabic-controlling Contract of Incorporation covering the corporate object (ISIC 6201 cloud vulnerability scanning and penetration testing SaaS), capital partition, profit-sharing ratio, management powers, audit provisions, dispute resolution, and liquidation rules. Arrange for execution of the deed before the notary by all founding shareholders or their attorney-in-fact, ensuring signature authentication and notary registration markings are affixed.
required_dossiers: Final draft Contract of Incorporation (Arabic-language original)
Valid passports and national IDs of all shareholders and managers
Notarized powers of attorney for any representative signatories
GAFI name reservation certificate
Declaration of capital adequacy for the stated corporate object
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises defects such as missing signatures, deficient power of attorney, or unpaid stamp duties, the parties may cure the defect within the notary's notice period by executing a supplementary signature page or resubmitting corrected deed; notary fee assessments may be appealed to the competent Notary-General authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account and Deposit Cash Share Capital Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed Egyptian bank selected by the founders (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, or Commercial International Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized Contract of Incorporation and name reservation certificate to the chosen bank to open a temporary company account under the Company's name. Deposit the cash portion of the subscribed capital according to the capital table and obtain a bank capital deposit certificate for submission to GAFI. For in-kind contributions, arrange a certified valuation report to support the capital allocation.
required_dossiers: Notarized Contract of Incorporation
GAFI name reservation certificate
Capital table and schedule of cash contributions
Certified valuation report for any in-kind contribution
AML/KYC declarations and beneficial ownership forms executed by shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines account opening under its internal AML risk policy, the founders may approach another licensed Egyptian bank or provide enhanced due diligence documentation (sources of wealth and funds) to the bank's AML compliance unit; refusal by one bank does not preclude incorporation filing with GAFI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Dossier with GAFI and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Company Registration Department at the Investor Services Center (One-Stop-Shop)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Compile the full incorporation dossier and submit it through the GAFI portal or Investor Services Center window. Pay the statutory filing and commercial registration fees. GAFI will verify the corporate object, capital structure, management appointments, and compliance with public order; upon approval, GAFI issues the Certificate of Incorporation and simultaneously records the Company in the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: Notarized Contract of Incorporation and notary authentication certificate
GAFI name reservation certificate
Bank capital deposit certificate or in-kind valuation report
Passport/national ID copies of shareholders and managers
Signed GAFI application form and authorized representative designation
Power of attorney granting formation authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deficiency query or refusal, the applicant must respond within 15 days by submitting an amended deed or supplementary declaration; a formal refusal may be appealed to GAFI's Internal Grievance Committee within 60 days and thereafter to the competent Administrative Court within the prescribed judicial time limit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax Registration: Tax Card, VAT and E-Invoicing Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Taxpayer Services Center and the competent tax office of the Company's jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the obtained Certificate of Incorporation and commercial registration extract with the ETA to obtain the Tax Card covering corporate income tax, payroll tax, withholding tax, and value-added tax. Register for VAT upon reaching or expecting an annual taxable turnover of EGP 500,000, with voluntary registration permitted for export-oriented SaaS services. Enroll in the ETA e-invoicing and e-receipt systems for business-to-business transactions and maintain payroll and withholding registrations.
required_dossiers: GAFI Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial registration extract current status
Lease contract for the registered office and civil defense fire safety certificate
Passport/national ID copies of managers and tax representative
Bank account confirmation letter
Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA requires supplementary attestation such as certified translation or verification of foreign shareholder documents, the applicant may submit the additional documents within 10 business days; classification disputes over tax obligations may be resolved by written request to the competent tax office and, if denied, by appeal before the ETA Internal Appeal Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Registrations: Social Insurance, Office License, Civil Defense and ICT/Data Protection Notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance, municipal district license office, Civil Defense Administration, and Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) through its agencies for optional ICT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Company as an employer with the local social insurance office and enroll all staff. Obtain a municipal commercial license for the office premises and arrange a Civil Defense fire-safety inspection covering egress, extinguishers, and electrical safety. Because the Company is a pure cloud cybersecurity SaaS provider, no industrial or environmental operating permit is required; however, if the Company plans to export ICT services or host infrastructure, it should register with the relevant MCIT/ITIDA platforms and, where personal data processing is conducted, notify the Office for Personal Data Protection under Law No. 151 of 2020.
required_dossiers: GAFI Certificate of Incorporation and ETA Tax Card
Office lease contract and building safety records
National ID/passport copies of employees
Social insurance registration forms
Civil Defense inspection request and floor plan of premises
MCIT/ITIDA registration form and data protection notification (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiency notices issued by the municipal district or Civil Defense may be cured by implementing the physical corrective actions (signage, fire extinguishers, egress clearance, minor layout modification) within 14 days and requesting re-inspection; any administrative refusal may be challenged before the Governorate Grievance Committee or the competent administrative court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; the ISIC 6201 cybersecurity SaaS activity is a pure digital service requiring no industrial manufacturing permit. If the Company later establishes a data center, server lab, or telecom infrastructure, the Industrial Development Authority and the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority would exercise jurisdiction over the relevant physical installation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; a standard municipal commercial license for the office premises suffices. An added telecom or value-added cybersecurity network license from the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority would be required only if the Company provides licensed managed telecom or hosted network security services in the public telecommunications sector.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) functioning under Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended by Laws No. 9 of 2009 and No. 202 of 2020
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / White List Category D for software development, office, and cloud-service activities; no full EIA report or environmental permit is required for the registered office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, volatile organic compound, or process emissions arise from cloud SaaS operations. If future on-site backup power or cooling equipment is installed, any diesel generator must comply with EEAA air emission thresholds under Decree No. 460 of 2006, and end-of-life IT hardware must be handed to EEAA-licensed e-waste recyclers under the hazardous waste management rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Administration fire-safety certificate and egress approval are required for the leased office; structural load inspection applies only where the Company constructs building alterations, which is not anticipated for a stand-alone SaaS operation. Occupational workplace clearance from the Ministry of Manpower labor inspection directorate is required to verify electrical safety, first-aid provisions, working-space adequacy, and employee health for computer-based labor.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance — unified tax and e-services portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing/e-receipts portal at https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; foreign investment incorporation and company formation handled by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Egyptian LLC: (1) incorporate through GAFI and obtain the Commercial Registry extract and investment file; (2) file ETA Form 1 (for legal persons) applying for the unified Tax Card/TIN, attaching the commercial registry extract, articles of association, board resolution, notarized power of attorney to the local manager, passport copies of directors, office lease, and bank account certificate — issuance generally takes 10-30 business days; (3) register for VAT under Law 67/2016 once the statutory threshold is exceeded or immediately upon commencing zero-rated export services, and obtain the VAT registration certificate; (4) enroll in the ETA e-invoicing platform and procure ETA-approved digital signing certificates for authorized signatories; (5) non-resident electronic-service suppliers without an Egyptian permanent establishment must obtain a simplified foreign-service-provider VAT registration with a dedicated TIN directly through the ETA electronic portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box, pass-through, or hybrid-mismatch election is available under Egyptian law; an LLC is an autonomous taxable person for corporate income tax (standard rate 22.5% under Law 30/2023) and for VAT. The only materially relevant election is the optional unified/simplified tax regime for small businesses with annual turnover not exceeding EGP 20 million, electable on the annual return, replacing accounting-based profit tax with a gross-receipts percentage (statutory band of 0.4%-1.5% by activity type). No fiscal unity, consolidation, or elective foreign-tax-credit pooling exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended by Law No. 3 of 2021 and Law No. 30 of 2023; place-of-supply and reverse-charge provisions govern cloud and cybersecurity SaaS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration when annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000 (Law 67/2016, Art. 15); voluntary registration available for annual turnover above EGP 50,000; non-resident suppliers of electronic services must register under the foreign-service-provider scheme with no Egyptian turnover threshold once they supply Egyptian consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance applies to all VAT registrants: e-invoices must be transmitted to the ETA e-invoicing platform via REST API/ERP integration using ETA-defined JSON schemas, or via the ETA web portal for smaller taxpayers; every invoice is validated in near real time and returned with a UUID and QR code (digital stamp) that together constitute the legal invoice; input VAT deduction, refund claims, and export zero-rating are conditional on cleared, error-free e-invoices; B2C sales additionally require QR-coded e-receipts through the separate e-receipt platform; non-compliance blocks deduction and exposes the taxpayer to statutory fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) is available under Art. 32 of Law 67/2016 for services supplied to a non-resident recipient for use and enjoyment wholly outside Egypt. For cybersecurity SaaS the exporter must substantiate: (i) the customer is a non-resident without an Egyptian establishment; (ii) the cloud platform is accessed and consumed outside Egypt (supported by IP geolocation and usage logs); (iii) invoices are issued in convertible foreign currency and the proceeds are actually credited to an Egyptian bank account; and (iv) the zero-rated supply is transmitted through the ETA e-invoicing system with the statutory export/zero-rating code. Input VAT apportioned to zero-rated exports is creditable, and excess credits are refundable through the ETA electronic refund procedure after documentary review.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (physical goods only; not applicable to pure SaaS — for services: signed SaaS subscription agreement, statement of work, and ETA-accepted service-export declaration)

Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (physical goods only; for SaaS: certificate of incorporation or tax-residence certificate of the non-resident customer, plus remote delivery and usage logs proving consumption outside Egypt)
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the Egyptian bank evidencing receipt of the foreign-currency consideration on the LLC's account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA subjects export zero-rating claims to heightened documentary audit, verifying the foreign beneficiary's existence, the economic substance of the SaaS delivery, and the matching of foreign-currency inflows to specific e-invoices. Deficient documentation triggers reclassification to the domestic 14% VAT rate, denial of input-credit refunds, assessment of VAT, delay fines at 2% per month (capped at 100% of the tax), and retrospective clawback of refunds within the statutory limitation period. Fraudulent or forged export and refund claims additionally attract an administrative penalty of not less than 30% and up to 100% of the tax evaded under Art. 75 of Law 67/2016, plus imprisonment of up to 5 years for tax evasion, with joint and several liability imposed on the LLC's managers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sole regulator for banking, foreign-exchange administration, and AML/CFT supervision, acting under Law No. 194 of 2020 (as amended by Law No. 88 of 2022) and the CBE Unified Banking Guidance. Exchange-control functions are executed through CBE-licensed Egyptian banks, with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) responsible for inward capital registration and the Egyptian Tax Authority for tax-clearance verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Following the exchange-rate unification of March 2024 under the IMF-supported reform programme, the EGP operates as a managed float and the parallel-market premium has been eliminated. Current-account convertibility is liberally permitted: SaaS and cybersecurity service export receipts may be credited in USD/EUR, and payments for imported cloud infrastructure and overseas software tools may be disbursed through licensed banks on documentary support. Capital-account convertibility for FDI is administratively open: equity injection, profit remittance, and liquidation proceeds are transferable after GAFI registration, CBE inflow reconciliation, audited financial statements, and a valid tax-clearance certificate are produced. The residual hurdles are documentary and institutional: banks apply strict source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership controls, and large remittances may be operationally deferred while CBE exchange-control codes are reconciled.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All service and software export proceeds must be repatriated through an Egyptian licensed bank within the contractual credit period benchmarked by banks at 90–180 days from invoice date; extensions require bank-level exchange-control approval. The post-March-2024 unified-rate regime has ended the blanket five-business-day conversion quotas previously applied during the 2022–2023 liquidity squeeze (50%, later raised); the LLC may now retain USD export proceeds in its USD account and convert into EGP at the interbank rate as operational needs require. Mandatory full surrender remains limited to state-designated strategic commodity exporters (petroleum, gold, fertilizers) and is inapplicable to an ISIC 6201 software exporter. Every inflow must nevertheless be reported under the CBE BPM6 purpose-code reconciliation framework and matched to the LLC's export registration file.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operational Current Account + Temporary Capital Deposit Account for LLC registration and GAFI documentation
USD Operational Current Account + EGP Current Account for payroll and domestic opex
Multi-currency USD/EGP Corporate Account with e-FX, corporate cards, and payments-API integration
Corporate multi-currency account linked to the HSBC global network for cross-border SaaS collections
USD/EGP Operational Account with trade-finance and documentary-credit desk
USD/EGP Account optimized for regional export invoice discounting and FX forwards
USD Operational Account for Gulf-route settlement of subscription invoices

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury. The CBE compels all export proceeds to enter licensed onshore bank accounts; offshore EMI accounts (Wise, Mercury, Revolut Business, Payoneer) are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in Egypt and fail the mandatory repatriation audit trail. They may be used only as auxiliary collection rails for low-value international card payments (e.g., Stripe or aggregator payout wallets), provided the reconciliation file ties each EMI payout to an underlying SaaS invoice and the funds are swept to the Egyptian USD account within the same settlement cycle. Legal constraint: retaining subscription revenue offshore beyond the bank-approved credit period without CBE registration is an exchange-control breach and will trigger source-of-funds scrutiny at account opening and during audits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Standard Egyptian practice mandates physical appearance of the general manager, one signatory director, and the shareholder-nominated legal representative at the branch with the original commercial register extract, notarized company by-laws, tax card, and specimen signatures. Banks with digital corporate onboarding (CIB, NBE Digital) accept a secure video interview only for the second director; fully remote opening is not recognized. For non-resident shareholders, the board resolution and Power of Attorney must be notarized and legalized through the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant Egyptian consulate/embassy, and passport copies, proof of address, and UBO identification must be filed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity — the bank applies a >10% beneficial-ownership threshold and demands the complete shareholding chain of the LLC, including the ultimate individuals behind the parent entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amended Memorandum of Association and share register, corporate-chain diagram, passport and CRS/FATCA self-certification of every UBO, and a compliance statement issued by the incorporating law firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds insufficiency for the initial USD capital injection — the investor's wealth and the business rationale of a cybersecurity SaaS in Egypt must be evidenced.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investor bank statement and inbound SWIFT MT103, capital-increase resolution, audited ultimate-entity financials, 12-month cash-flow model, and GAFI approval receipt under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, embargo, and dual-use exposure — subscriptions from clients in high-risk or embargoed jurisdictions may classify the penetration-testing software as a dual-use cyber capability.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UN/EU/OFAC/Arab League screening results for the client base, end-user attestation certificates, accepted-use annexes in subscription contracts, and written confirmation from EG-CERT where export-control assessment is requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity or mismatched transactions — Stripe aggregator payouts or trailing cloud-cost payments without invoice linkage and e-invoicing records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited SaaS revenue schedule with payment-gateway payout reports, reconciled bank statements, CBE export-file invoices, and proof of electronic-invoice reporting to the Egyptian Tax Authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-filing mismatch — the bank's tax-clearance check finds arrears, non-registration, or non-compliance with the VAT/e-invoicing databases.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid tax-clearance certificate issued by the Ministry of Finance, latest CIT and VAT returns, an updated Tax Card for the ISIC 6201 activity, and the LLC's e-invoicing platform registration PIN.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The investor must wire USD/EUR via SWIFT MT103 to the LLC's USD account at the Egyptian relationship bank, referencing the CBE inward-remittance code for direct investment in share capital and the LLC's registered identification. The bank issues an inward remittance receipt matched to the notarized by-laws and a capital deposit certificate before GAFI finalizes its investment approval; funds may remain in USD or be converted to EGP at the unified interbank midpoint. Wire amounts above USD 250,000 require source-of-funds documentation, AML clearance, and confirmation that the sending institution is an approved correspondent of the receiving Egyptian bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The standard clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for trade and service settlements — including invoice-backed payments to cloud hyperscalers and international SaaS tooling — processed through the bank's CBE service-import registration module and the LLC's e-invoicing file. For procurement of scanning appliances or hardware, a documentary credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) with a confirmed Egyptian advising bank is applied, including ACID/CargoX pre-shipment registration under the Customs Law No. 207 of 2020. Corporate Visa/Mastercard is permissible for recurring low-value global subscriptions with an internal monthly limit and automated reconciliation against invoice files.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward (CBE-approved banks only; maximum 12-month tenor, strictly collateralized by documented export receivables or import liabilities of the SaaS business)
Full-delivery USD/EGP FX swap for rolling operational liquidity covering payroll and domestic tax-funding requirements
USD/EGP cross-currency swap for term-lending exposure, subject to CBE derivative-product eligibility assessments

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) on EGP eligible only as a mirror hedge arranged between the bank's offshore group desk and its Egyptian branch; direct offshore NDF speculation by the Egyptian resident is not permitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Commercial Registry Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January of each calendar year, regardless of incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a penalty of 10% of the annual fee per month up to 100%; renewal refused after one year leads to suspension of commercial registration, administrative strike-off, and loss of standing to execute banking or customs transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end, i.e., by 30 April for a calendar-year taxpayer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed payment is charged a 2% monthly surcharge on unpaid tax for each commenced month, plus fixed administrative fines of EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000; non-filing empowers ETA to issue a deemed assessment and enforce compulsory collection, including bank garnishment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - UBO Register, coordinated with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January together with the Commercial Register renewal, and within 30 days after any shareholding transfer or UBO change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the UBO confirmation subjects the responsible manager to fines of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 under the AML legal framework; undisclosed share transfers are unenforceable against third parties and may block corporate dividend distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payroll and Withholding Tax Aggregate Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January of each year for the preceding calendar year, reconciling all monthly payroll declarations already filed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late reconciliation triggers a 2% monthly surcharge on outstanding payroll tax and creates joint personal liability of the manager for under-withheld amounts; material discrepancies may lead to reassessment of deducted expenses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Audited Annual Financial Statements with GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies File
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end, i.e., by 30 June for calendar-year accounts, following the Ordinary General Assembly approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-deposit obstructs the forthcoming Commercial Register renewal and exposes the general manager to fines of EGP 1,000 to EGP 5,000; knowingly filing false financials is treated as a criminal misrepresentation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is compulsory for every Egyptian LLC irrespective of size under Companies Law No. 159/1981; the Ordinary General Assembly must appoint one or more independent certified public accountants before the end of January of the financial year. No turnover, asset, or capital threshold exempts an LLC from audit, although micro-enterprises validly registered under Law No. 17/2018 may obtain a practitioner review in place of a full audit only where explicitly permitted by GAFI and the Egyptian Tax Authority.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), as issued by the Egyptian Society of Accountants and Auditors and applied by the Egyptian Tax Authority; EAS are substantively IFRS-converged. Full IFRS is accepted for foreign-owned subsidiaries and consolidated reporting when accompanied by EAS reconciliation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egypt's Law No. 15/2021 amending the Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2002 requires every LLC to maintain a beneficial ownership register and to file it with GAFI. An annual confirmation is submitted no later than 31 January, coinciding with the Commercial Register renewal. Any shareholding transfer, capital increase, or redemption must be recorded in the company's register of members and a revised UBO statement filed within 30 days. The manager must sign a statutory declaration identifying every natural person directly or indirectly holding or controlling 10% or more of the equity or voting power, as required under applicable AML Executive Regulations; the UBO confirmation must attach the updated list of shareholders.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 0 if the LLC maintains its own Egyptian physical registered address; USD 2,800 to USD 5,000 per annum for a GAFI-accredited corporate service agent providing a Cairo registered office, commercial register renewal processing, UBO secretarial administration, and statutory filing coordination.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 to USD 3,500 for a licensed Egyptian CPA firm auditing a cybersecurity SaaS LLC with one business line and EAS-only statutory accounts; add USD 1,000 to USD 1,800 if the engagement includes consolidated IFRS reporting pack, transfer pricing documentation, or ETA defense support.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket statutory tax holiday for an onshore Egyptian LLC. Available incentives under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 may include a tax credit of up to 50% of certified investment costs for qualifying projects in priority or underdeveloped zones; free-zone licensed projects may substitute income tax with an annual levy of 1% of gross revenue; additionally, eligible cybersecurity and IT service exporters can access sectoral schemes allowing deduction of up to 30% of export revenues or R&D expenditures, subject to ETA approval.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Tax Form No. 1 (Corporate Income Tax Return) under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-Tax portal at https://tax.gov.eg or https://etax.gov.eg.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the company's fiscal/tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 30 April; for a 30 June year-end, the deadline is 31 October.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, tax identification number (TIN), address, legal form, capital, fiscal year start and end dates, zone or governorate code and branch data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must register through the ETA foreign taxpayer desk, obtain an Egyptian TIN, attach a notarised power of attorney to the Egyptian tax agent, and provide foreign tax ID and treaty residence details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 1, Part C – Revenue Boxes (e.g., C.1, C.2, C.3)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate annual turnover comprising SaaS subscription fees, cloud security services, vulnerability scanning proceeds, penetration testing fees, maintenance and support revenue, and other operating income, reconciled to audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must report only Egypt-source income. Cryptographically delivered SaaS or cybersecurity services are sourced by reference to the place of use/exploitation of the service under Egyptian income tax rules; taxpayer should attach customer site lists and electronic usage evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 1, Part D – Deductions and Adjustments (e.g., D.1, D.2, D.3)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct and indirect costs: employee costs, third-party cloud infrastructure, software licences, royalties, rent, utility costs, depreciation, amortisation, legal and audit fees, and financial charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident with a permanent establishment in Egypt may allocate documented head-office and internal services expenses only in accordance with OECD-compatible attribution rules and must file an annual cost-apportionment statement with ETA; no direct deduction is permitted to a non-resident without a PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 1, Part E – Tax Computation (e.g., E.1, E.2, E.3)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after disallowances and loss carryforward; application of the 22.5% statutory rate; deduction of advance payments and withholding tax credits; final balance payable, refund due or carryover.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents should compute tax in Egyptian pounds, apply only treaty-reduced rates after an approved ETA DTA relief application, and attach the relevant tax residency certificate and beneficial ownership declaration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an immediate administrative penalty of EGP 500; each commenced month of delayed filing adds a penalty of up to 2% of the total tax liability for the year, capped at 25% of that tax. Late payment of assessed tax accrues monthly surcharge of 1.5% of the unpaid amount, and criminal fines up to EGP 50,000 may apply if the return is knowingly filed with false particulars.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (final withholding tax on cash or in-kind dividends distributed by an Egyptian LLC to its shareholders, including non-resident shareholders, unless a zero-rate participation exemption applies to qualifying corporate shareholders holding at least 25% of the paying company and meeting Egyptian legal substance conditions).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced dividend, interest or royalty withholding rate under a double taxation agreement (DTA), the beneficial owner or payer must submit a DTA relief application on the ETA designated form along with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, an explanatory memorandum detailing the commercial purpose, underlying agreements, board resolution, shareholding proof and evidence of beneficial ownership. The ETA must issue an approval or reduced-withholding instruction before the payment is made; otherwise the statutory rate is withheld at source and a refund is recoverable only through the formal objection or refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 20% withholding tax on interest and 20% withholding tax on royalties paid to non-residents. Under most Egyptian tax treaties these rates are reduced to 10% for royalties and 0-15% for interest depending on the treaty, the beneficial ownership of the payment, and the nature of the intangible or debt claim. Technical fees and payments for cybersecurity software licensing may be recharacterised as royalties by the ETA based on the substance of the transfer of rights.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory local file and master file documentation is required where (i) the aggregate value of controlled transactions with related parties exceeds EGP 15 million in a tax year, or (ii) total annual turnover of the Egyptian entity exceeds EGP 20 million; country-by-country reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue equal to or above EUR 750 million. The documentation must be submitted within 30 days of a formal ETA request, with a contemporaneous TP master file maintained annually.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to the Gulf jurisdictions. However, the Egyptian Tax Authority enforces a substance-over-form doctrine under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in Article 91 of Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, and may disregard, recharacterise or reallocate transactions that lack commercial rationale or economic substance. In particular, entities claiming treaty benefits, participation exemption or controlled foreign company reliefs must demonstrate real operational substance (personnel, management, physical or tangible infrastructure, risk control and principal purpose of profit-making).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Suppressed or Falsified Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting SaaS subscription receipts from the annual return, using an unregistered foreign payment processor (e.g., an offshore Stripe account) to avoid Egyptian bank controls, issuing fake or inflated invoices to Egyptian clients, or booking personal foreign bank deposits as deferred revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for a term of up to 5 years and/or a fine of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000; unpaid tax remains due with monthly interest surcharge of 1.5%; in egregious cases the tax authority may impose an additional penalty of up to 100% of the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, signatories and actual managers who prepared or signed false returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, interest and penal surcharges. Criminal conviction triggers a travel ban, disqualification from board service and asset freezes against personal bank accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Statutory and Cross-Border WHT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident shareholder without deducting the 10% dividend withholding tax, or failing to withhold 20% on cross-border royalties and interest paid to a foreign cloud security licensor or lender; also includes attempting to recharacterise SaaS licence fees as tax-free service fees to evade WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Egyptian LLC is held as statutory withholding agent and assessed for the unremitted tax; monetary penalty of up to 25% of the withheld amount and monthly late interest of 1.5% apply; deliberate non-withholding may escalate to criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director, finance director and tax compliance officer may be made personally responsible for the gross WHT deficiency and penalties; ETA imposes personal travel restrictions and may block bank accounts of the responsible directors while restitution is ongoing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mismatch – Abusive Profit Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing intra-group technical support, cybersecurity platform licences or software development fees at artificial below-arm's-length margins; treating Egyptian revenue as compensating a foreign related party with no functional or risk analysis; failing to maintain or file local file/master file after exceeding the EGP 15 million transaction threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may compute a transfer pricing adjustment to the taxable base; an additional tax of up to 40% of the additionally assessed tax is imposed, plus monthly interest of 1.5% on the deficiency; failure to provide contemporaneous documentation is penalised separately by fines up to between EGP 20,000 and EGP 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or executed the non-arm's-length cross-border agreements are jointly liable for the adjusted tax and penalty amounts; the ETA may issue domestic enforcement warnings, travel bans and, in deliberate or fraudulent cases, refer the directors to criminal court for aiding tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Egyptian LLC as a paper treasury or conduit vessel with no real personnel, premises, effective management, server assets or principal economic activity in Egypt, designed solely to access treaty benefits on outbound royalty/dividend flows or to claim the participation exemption for the benefit of non-resident principals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the General Anti-Avoidance Rule resulting in recharacterisation of the transaction, denial of treaty benefits, reinstatement of the whole taxable profit in the hands of the Egyptian entity, and penalty assessment up to 100% of the additional taxes; commercial licence revocation may follow under the Investment Law. Egypt also reserves anti-conduit and beneficial ownership clauses under its DTAs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors who structured or maintained the artificial arrangement may be held jointly and severally liable for the entire avoided tax plus penalties; they face travel bans, restriction on initiating insolvency proceedings, disqualification as directors, and imprisonment where their manipulation involved forged residency certificates or fabricated service contracts.
